messages.content:
You are FOXO's lifestyle coach. Using the doctor's review of a member's lab results, write a practical diet and lifestyle plan for a member living in India.

Rules:
1. Respect the member's diet, allergies and conditions in every item:
   - vegetarian: no meat, fish, seafood or eggs
   - eggetarian: eggs are fine; no meat, fish or seafood
   - vegan: no animal products, including dairy, ghee and honey
   - jain: vegetarian with no eggs, no honey, no onion or garlic, and no root vegetables (potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar)
   - allergies: never include the allergen in any form
   - diabetes: no sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets or sweetened drinks
2. Each diet recommendation must target one of the abnormal biomarkers in the doctor's findings. Put that biomarker's name in linked_biomarker, written as in the findings.
3. Never contradict the doctor's lifestyle_restrictions. If the doctor restricts exercise, suggest only gentle activity such as an easy walk, and tell the member to follow the doctor's advice.
4. Do not recommend medicines or supplements and never give doses. If a supplement might help, say "ask your FOXO doctor".
5. Use everyday Indian foods (dal, millets, seasonal sabzi, sprouts and so on) and be specific about portions and timing.
6. Put foods to eat in diet_recommendations and foods to limit or avoid in foods_to_avoid.
7. retest_in_weeks is usually 12.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"DietRecommendation": {"properties": {"item": {"title": "Item", "type": "string"}, "rationale": {"title": "Rationale", "type": "string"}, "linked_biomarker": {"title": "Linked Biomarker", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["item", "rationale", "linked_biomarker"], "title": "DietRecommendation", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"focus_areas": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Focus Areas", "type": "array"}, "diet_recommendations": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DietRecommendation"}, "title": "Diet Recommendations", "type": "array"}, "foods_to_avoid": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Foods To Avoid", "type": "array"}, "activity": {"title": "Activity", "type": "string"}, "sleep": {"title": "Sleep", "type": "string"}, "retest_in_weeks": {"title": "Retest In Weeks", "type": "integer"}}, "required": ["focus_areas", "diet_recommendations", "activity", "sleep", "retest_in_weeks"], "title": "CoachPlan", "type": "object"}

response: {"focus_areas":["Improve fasting glucose and HbA1c with low-glycaemic, high-fibre vegetarian meals","Lower LDL and total cholesterol with soluble fibre and heart-healthy fats","Reduce triglycerides by limiting refined carbohydrates, sweets, and fried foods","Build regular activity and sleep routines to support metabolic health"],"diet_recommendations":[{"item":"At lunch and dinner, fill half the plate with non-starchy seasonal sabzi (lauki, bhindi, palak, cabbage, beans), one quarter with whole dal/rajma/chana, and one quarter with one bajra/jowar/ragi roti or 1/2 cup cooked brown rice.","rationale":"This plate portion controls refined carbohydrate intake and adds fibre, which supports lower fasting glucose.","linked_biomarker":"glucose_fasting"},{"item":"Eat breakfast within 1–2 hours of waking: 1 small bowl (30 g dry) steel-cut oats or 1 ragi roti with unsweetened curd/paneer and a vegetable; avoid fruit juice and sweet tea/coffee.","rationale":"A low-sugar, high-fibre breakfast and consistent meal timing help steady blood glucose and support HbA1c improvement.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"Finish dinner by 8:00–8:30 pm and keep a 12-hour overnight fast (for example, 8:30 pm to 8:30 am); avoid snacks after dinner.","rationale":"Earlier dinner and overnight fasting can improve glucose control and support lower HbA1c.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"Include 1 bowl (about 150 g cooked) of soluble-fibre-rich legumes such as chana, rajma, lobia, or black-eyed beans 4–5 times a week.","rationale":"Soluble fibre from legumes helps bind cholesterol and supports lowering LDL cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"},{"item":"Use 1–2 teaspoons of mustard, rice bran, or olive oil per meal and choose low-fat dairy; keep ghee/butter small and avoid deep-fried foods.","rationale":"Replacing saturated and fried fats with measured heart-healthy oils helps reduce total cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"total_cholesterol"},{"item":"Replace biscuits/namkeen with 1 small handful (20 g) unsalted nuts or 1 bowl of moong/kala chana sprouts; have whole fruit such as guava or apple instead of juice.","rationale":"Lower refined-carbohydrate and added-sugar intake helps reduce triglycerides.","linked_biomarker":"triglycerides"}],"foods_to_avoid":["Sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets, desserts, and sweetened drinks","Soft drinks, packed fruit juices, and sweetened tea/coffee","Refined flour (maida) items such as white bread, naan, biscuits, cakes, and bakery products","Deep-fried and packaged snacks such as samosa, pakora, puri, namkeen, and chips","Large amounts of ghee, butter, vanaspati, and repeated/reheated frying oil"],"activity":"Aim for 150 minutes per week of moderate activity such as brisk walking, plus 10–15 minutes of easy walking after lunch and dinner. Follow your doctor's advice if any exercise restriction is given; in that case, keep to gentle walking only.","sleep":"Target 7–8 hours of sleep nightly, with regular sleep and wake times; avoid screens for 30 minutes before bed.","retest_in_weeks":12}
